takeaways: Clean blowout: non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.38 vs $0.34 expected, and revenue of $782.5 million, up 39% year over year, vs $736.8 million (Investing.com). Fastest revenue growth in nearly four years, per the company.
GAAP still loses money: GAAP net loss of $34.1 million, or $0.10 per share, vs a $1.3 million loss a year ago. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 17.5% from 15.3%.

Guidance is well above the Street: Q4 revenue $845-$846 million vs ~$798.2 million expected, Q4 non-GAAP EPS $0.43 vs $0.38, and full-year revenue $2.963-$2.964 billion vs ~$2.87 billion with non-GAAP EPS of $1.35 vs $1.26 (Investing.com).
Current RPO grew 37% year over year. Free cash flow was $82.1 million (10% of revenue), and cash plus securities sat at $5.13 billion.
Investing.com reported the stock surging over 17% after hours; Yahoo Finance showed it around $280 vs a $244.51 regular-session close.
verdict: Cloudflare just posted its 'best quarter ever,' which is CEO-speak for 'we accidentally printed money and then guided like we meant to.' It beat, it raised, and after hours the stock is doing cardio. GAAP still loses a dime a share, but Wall Street is pricing the AI connectivity story, not the stock-based-comp hangover.
